t: Design Exam Scores Tracker — Prefix Sums + Binary Search
o: Records arrive with strictly increasing times, and queries never reference the future. Keeping times in an array and a running prefix sum of scores lets any interval total be answered as prefix(upTo endTime) − prefix(before startTime) via two binary searches. Example: after records at times 1 (98) and 5 (99), totalScore(1,5) = 197 while totalScore(3,4) = 0.
k: Chronological inserts mean a flat array + prefix sums suffices — no balanced BST needed.
Each query is two binary searches: lower_bound(startTime) and upper_bound(endTime).

a.i: Append each record to a times array and extend a prefix-score array. A query sums scores of records with startTime ≤ t ≤ endTime by locating the index range with binary search.
s: record: push time; push last prefix + score.
totalScore: l = first index with time ≥ startTime; r = first index with time > endTime.
Return pre[r] − pre[l] (0 when the range is empty).
a.t: O(log n) per query, O(1) amortized per record — binary searches dominate
a.sp: O(n) for times and prefix sums

w: This is the canonical solution; there is no meaningfully different second approach worth coding. Pitfalls: using bisect_right for the left boundary (double-counting startTime), and integer overflow of score sums in Java/C++ (use 64-bit). Follow-up: support deletions or out-of-order inserts (would require a BIT over coordinates).
